title: Modelling exponential growth
keyIdea: An exponential model y = a · bᵗ describes something that is multiplied by the same factor b in every equal time step, starting from a at t = 0. From a description, a is the starting amount, b = 1 + r/100 for growth of r% per step, and t counts the steps the rate is given for, measured from the start. From two data points, divide the later value by the earlier one to get bⁿ for n steps, take the nth root for b, then divide back to t = 0 to find a. Use the model to predict by substituting t, and then judge the answer: real growth runs into limits such as food, space or the number of people, so exponential models work only over limited ranges.
familyTip: Pick a savings account or a phone game that boosts points by a percentage. Together, write its model as start × factorᵗ, predict the value after five steps, then check it on a calculator. Ask: could this keep going for fifty steps? What would stop it?

visual.caption: Match each description to its growth factor b. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: keeps 95% of its value each year

lab.caption: Flagship lab: fit b to data, build a · bᵗ from stories, predict with the model, judge whether a prediction is reasonable, and fit a model from two points.

kid: An exponential model is y = a · bᵗ. The start value a is the amount when t = 0. The factor b is what you multiply by in one time step. The number t counts the steps.
Growth of r% in each step means b = 1 + r/100. So 4% a year gives b = 1.04, and tripling gives b = 3. If a town has 12,000 people in 2018, then t is the years since 2018. For 2030, t = 12, not 2030.

Two points can give the model. Say y is 450 when t = 2 and 1518.75 when t = 5. Divide: 1518.75 ÷ 450 = 3.375. That is b³, since the points are 3 steps apart. The cube root gives b = 1.5. Then go back 2 steps: 450 ÷ 1.5² = 200, so a = 200.

To predict, put the time into the model. £500 at 4% gives 500 · 1.04⁹ ≈ £712 after 9 years. Then ask if the answer makes sense. A virus can't grow by 25% a week for two years. There are not enough people.
adult: Ages 15 to 17. The US Common Core asks students to build exponential functions from a description of a relationship or from two input–output pairs (F-LE.2). It also asks them to write a function that models a situation (F-BF.1a). In England, GCSE Maths covers compound interest and growth and decay, and A level uses exponential models and their limits.

The method has three parts. Set t = 0 at the start of the story and choose the step the rate is per. Turn a percentage into a factor, b = 1 + r/100. With two points n steps apart, the ratio of the values is bⁿ, so b is its nth root. Then a is a known value divided by b to the power of its t. After predicting, test the size against the context.

Common mistakes: using the rate as the factor (0.04 or 4 instead of 1.04); putting the calendar year in for t; using the ratio over several steps as the factor for one step, as in b = 4 when 200 becomes 800 over two hours; dividing a rise by the number of steps instead of taking a root; leaving a as a value that is not at t = 0; treating compound growth as simple interest, so £500 at 4% is thought to take 10 years to pass £700; and trusting a long-range prediction that breaks real limits.

In the lab, students drag b until a curve fits three data sets, then build four models from stories, slot by slot. Next they drag a time marker to the first step that reaches a target. They judge six predictions as reasonable or broken. Last, they find b and then a from three pairs of points, none at t = 0.

practice.prompt: £800 is invested at 3% compound interest a year. Which model gives the value after t years?
practice.hint: Growth of r% multiplies by 1 + r/100 each year.
practice.explain: 3% growth is × 1.03 each year, so V = 800 · 1.03ᵗ. 0.03ᵗ would shrink the money, and adding gives a straight line.

practice.prompt: A colony starts at {a} cells and doubles every hour. Using y = a · 2ᵗ, how many cells are there after 3 hours?
A value is 150 at t = 0 and 216 at t = 2. What is b?
practice.hint: 216 ÷ 150 is b², because the points are 2 steps apart.
practice.explain: 216 ÷ 150 = 1.44 = b², so b = √1.44 = 1.2. 1.44 is the change over two steps, and 1.22 just halves the 44% rise.

practice.prompt: A town had 4,000 people in 2015 and grows by a factor of 1.1 each year. Write the model with t = years since 2015. What is t for the year {y}?
practice.hint: Count the years from the start, 2015.
practice.explain: t = {y} − 2015 = {=y-2015}. The model is P = 4000 · 1.1ᵗ, so you use t = {=y-2015}, not {y}.

practice.prompt: A model says a phone game will have 10¹² players in 3 years. What is the best comment?
choices: Unreasonable: that is far more than the people on Earth.
Fine, if the arithmetic is right.
practice.hint: Compare the answer with a real limit.
practice.explain: About 8 × 10⁹ people are alive, so 10¹² players is impossible. The model may fit early data, but limits stop the growth.

pool.prompt: Bacteria grow from 300 to 2700 in 2 hours. What is the hourly growth factor?
pool.hint: 2700 ÷ 300 is the change over 2 hours, which is b².
pool.explain: 2700 ÷ 300 = 9 = b², so b = 3. 9 is the 2-hour factor, and 4.5 halves 9 instead of taking the root.

pool.prompt: £500 at 4% compound interest a year. After how many whole years does it first pass £700?
pool.hint: Work out 500 · 1.04ᵗ for t = 8 and t = 9.
pool.explain: 500 · 1.04⁸ ≈ £684 and 500 · 1.04⁹ ≈ £712, so 9 years. Thinking 40% ÷ 4% = 10 treats it as simple interest.

pool.prompt: A value is 1100 at t = 1 and 1331 at t = 3. What is a?
pool.hint: Find b first, then go back one step from t = 1.
pool.explain: 1331 ÷ 1100 = 1.21 = b², so b = 1.1. Then a = 1100 ÷ 1.1 = 1000. 1100 is the value at t = 1, and 909 divides by b twice.

pool.prompt: A video has {v} views and the views triple every day. Using y = {v} · 3ᵗ, how many views after 2 days?
pool.hint: Each day multiplies by 3, so 2 days multiply by 3² = 9.

pool.prompt: Cases of a disease are 40 and rise 25% a week. Which model fits?
pool.explain: Start 40, factor 1.25 per week. Using 25 as the factor, or swapping a and b, gives a different function.

pool.prompt: Which prediction from C = 40 · 1.25ᵗ is most reasonable to trust?
pool.hint: Short ranges are safest. Check sizes against real limits.
pool.explain: 40 · 1.25³ ≈ 78 is close to the data. After 100 weeks the model gives more cases than people alive, and 40 weeks is far outside the data too.

pool.prompt: A model is y = {a} · 1.5ᵗ. What is y when t = 2?
pool.hint: Square the factor first: 1.5² = 2.25, then multiply by a.

pool.prompt: A population triples every 2 years. What is the yearly factor?
pool.hint: Two years of growth is b², and that must equal 3.
pool.explain: b² = 3, so b = √3 ≈ 1.73. 1.5 shares the tripling out by dividing, and 3 is the factor for two years.

pool.prompt: Why does 2000 · 1.05ᵗ grow faster each year than 2000 + 100t?
choices: Each year's 5% is taken of a bigger amount.
pool.hint: Ask what the 5% is taken of each year: the start, or the new amount?
pool.explain: Compound growth takes 5% of the new, larger amount, so the yearly rise grows. Both start at 2000, and 2000 + 100t adds the same 100 every year.
